items.text: Panes no longer redraw their whole frame on every update after about 100,000 frames.
With NumLock or CapsLock on, moving the mouse or typing over a pane no longer redraws the whole screen on every event.
A loop window the user renames is still recognised as the loop.
The Windows performance audit now has one index of all 102 findings, each tied to a task, and the first re-audit is scheduled.
Terminal panes share one GPU device instead of each creating their own, so ten panes use 116 threads instead of 611.
A pane whose cursor cannot blink no longer redraws itself every 600 ms.
Frames where no link can light up no longer scan the whole screen for links.
Each frame uploads only the cell bytes that changed, in one call, instead of the whole screen row by row.
A new glyph no longer re-uploads the whole font atlas to every pane.
A pane gives back its graphics memory a second after its size settles, so a once-maximized window no longer holds maximized-size memory for life.
A pane on a background tab now gives back its GPU render targets, and every hidden release also frees the compositor's staging texture.
The first performance re-audit is in: this week's fixes cut memory and threads roughly in half, and nothing got worse.
